questions.question:
A statement is given followed by two arguments. Decide which of the arguments is/are strong with respect to the statement.

**Statement:**

The Government of State A is planning to shut down all markets by 7 pm.

**Arguments:**

I. Incidents of shoplifting and attempted robberies have increased especially during night time.

II. Many people get time to shop only after office hours.

options.text: Both I and II strengthen the statement.
I weakens while II strengthens the statement.
Both I and II weaken the statement.
II weakens while I strengthens the statement.

questions.solution:
Given statement: The Government of State A is planning to shut down all markets by 7 pm.

Given conclusions:

I. Incidents of shoplifting and attempted robberies have increased especially during night time → Strong

This argument provides a strong in favor of the decision, as shutting down markets earlier could help in reducing crime rates. Since safety and crime prevention are valid concerns for policy decisions, this argument is strong.

II. Many people get time to shop only after office hours → Weak

This argument highlights a practical issue against the decision. If markets close early, it could inconvenience working individuals, potentially affecting business as well. Since this argument does not directly challenge the purpose of the decision but only highlights a drawback.

Thus, argument **II weakens while I strengthens the statement.**

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Question: Five people A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Who sits second to the right of A?

Statement (I): The number of people sitting to the right of A is equal to the number of people sitting to the left of A. One person sits between A and B. D sits to the immediate left of B.

Statement (II): E sits at the extreme left end of the row. Only one person sits between E and A. B sits to the immediate right of D.

options.text: Data in statements I and II together are sufficient to answer the question.
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not.
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not.
Data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question.

questions.solution:
**Given: **Five people A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a straight row, facing north.

**Statement (I)**: The number of people sitting to the right of A is equal to the number of people sitting to the left of A. One person sits between A and B. D sits to the immediate left of B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ea1b8ee29ea400470374601bbd0dcbb27cc9bcfa1b0516b81cfeea34a509880.png] 

Here, B is second to the right of A.

So, Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question.

**Statement (II):** E sits at the extreme left end of the row. Only one person sits between E and A. B sits to the immediate right of D. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/782a15d61a68b09f11b788e2faaf4f5a399beac72ccda46d95666fe7bb1b32ed.png] 

Here, B is second to the right of A.

Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question .

Thus,** Data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**
